assertions: an unrecognizable timezone downgrades the time basis instead of being ignored
ESP facts with no shared key stay a low-confidence candidate, never a link

recommendedChecks: Re-collect both sides in one pass so they share an enrollment or correlation identifier.
Compare the Entra device id recorded by each side.
findings.summary: The supplied ESP session facts carry no enrollment, correlation, activity, or device identifier in common with the Autopilot evidence. They may describe the same provisioning attempt or a different one; proximity in time is not proof.
findings.title: ESP evidence exists but shares no identifier with the Autopilot evidence

recommendedChecks: Re-collect with the device's timezone recorded alongside the evidence.
Prefer sources that emit an explicit UTC offset per record.
findings.summary: Ordering fell back to record identity because the declared timezone is not a recognizable UTC offset or region identifier. No conclusion in this analysis relies on wall-clock time, and time-proximity correlation with an ESP session is refused outright.
findings.title: The capture declared an unrecognizable timezone

recommendedChecks: Review the correlated ESP session for what happened after the handoff.
findings.summary: A profile was retrieved and applied, and the handoff into enrollment and the Enrollment Status Page was observed. Everything after this point belongs to the ESP analysis, not to Autopilot.
findings.title: The local Autopilot phase completed and handed off
